text: My aunt counts on it year after year. She turns the house upside down for us; she invites our special friends—she scarcely knows Frieda, and we can’t leave her on her hands. I missed one day, and she would be so hurt if I didn’t stay the full ten.” “But I’ll say a word to her. Don’t you bother.” “Henry, I won’t go. Don’t bully me.” “You want to see the house, though?” “Very much—I’ve heard so much about it, one way or the other.
